concerns.concern: No series or contact resistance, normal-state resistance or normalization procedure is reported, and only normalized conductance in arbitrary units is shown. The peak heights that support the pz-component argument could therefore be artifacts of normalization.
concerns.quote: Not discussed. The peak heights of 1.70 and 2.08 (p. 8) carry the pz argument

concerns.concern: The contacts may not be ballistic. If so, the side dips and the zero-bias enhancement could be critical-current or heating effects rather than Andreev bound states. The authors should check the regime from R_N and the mean free path, and test whether the dips sit at fixed current.
concerns.quote: Integrate dI/dV to I(V) and test whether the side dips sit at fixed current in T. The 1.4 GPa dips move inward on warming (Fig. 3d)

concerns.concern: Under pressure, the contact may cover several regions with different gaps because of pressure inhomogeneity, which the authors raise but leave open. Parallel channels could mimic the features and the temperature minimum of the gap ratio in Fig. 5f.
concerns.quote: refit Fig. 5f with two channels to see whether the minimum stays

concerns.concern: All pressure data come from a single contact on sample S1. Neither a second pressurized contact nor a repeat on pressure release is shown, so the pressure-dependent features are not shown to be reproducible.
concerns.quote: all pressure data come from S1

concerns.concern: Magnetic or Kondo scattering is not ruled out as the source of the zero-bias peak under pressure. Field sweeps exist only at ambient pressure, and the dismissal relies on the absence of magnetic order at ambient pressure, which may not apply near the pressure-induced MO1 and MO2 phases.
concerns.quote: Take field sweeps at 0.6 to 1.4 GPa, closest to MO1 and MO2, and check whether the ZBCP splits

concerns.concern: It is unclear how robust the fitted ratio ⟨∆z⟩/⟨∆x(y)⟩ is to the choice of model. The 0.6 and 0.8 GPa data should be refit with two channels or with other pairing representations to see how much the ratio changes.
concerns.quote: how much does ⟨∆z⟩/⟨∆x(y)⟩ move when you refit the 0.6 and 0.8 GPa data with two channels or with the other representations?

concerns.concern: The gap labels for S1 are inconsistent between Table S1 and Fig. S7a: the values of ∆z and ∆x(y) are swapped for the same 0.3 K fit.
concerns.quote: Table S1 lists ∆z = 1.18(7) meV and ∆x(y) = 0.72(4) meV for S1, while Fig. S7a gives ∆x(y) = 1.18(7) meV

concerns.concern: The paper does not say how many point contacts were made at ambient pressure and in the pressure cell, how many showed the zero-bias peak, or why any were set aside. Selection of the shown data therefore cannot be judged.
concerns.quote: How many point contacts did you make on (0 0 1) surfaces, at ambient pressure and in the pressure cell, and how many showed a ZBCP?

concerns.concern: The measured ranges are incomplete or unexplained. There are no point-contact spectra above 1.4 GPa although the cell reaches about 1.8 GPa, no bias beyond ±4 mV is shown, and no reasons are given for the chosen ranges.
concerns.quote: no PCS above 1.4 GPa, although the cell reaches "∼ 1.8 GPa" (p. 11)

concerns.concern: The processing steps from raw data to figures, including normalization, are not given. Raw data and analysis code are not provided, despite the claim that all source data are in the paper.
concerns.quote: Normalization, raw data and code are not given.

concerns.concern: The results should be compared with related point-contact and STM work on UTe2, for example the much smaller py gap fitted by Yoon et al., and with literature on point-contact artifacts.
concerns.quote: A p-wave BTK fit gives a py gap of 0.26 ± 0.06 meV, a useful comparison for your fitted gap amplitudes.
